label: r4c3
name: Shared shift kernel, 2 epochs
hypothesis: Combines the shared shift kernel (candidate 1) with 2 PPO epochs. In r3c1, 2 epochs reached 0.77 on one seed but failed on the other, which looks like a slow, seed-dependent discovery of the shift. If a shared 8-weight shift makes alignment fast and reliable, both seeds should get the benefit of about 1.9x the samples. Refuted if mean dev success is not above 0.43, or if one seed again stays below 0.15.
last_analysis: Realigning the shifted target with a learned wrap-around full-row convolution is what made learning possible (the starting net and the transformer both stayed at 0). The cheap early-fusion version, r2c2, is best at 0.43 (0.31 and 0.54). r3c1 uses the same net with 2 PPO epochs and scored about the same mean (0.42), but one seed reached 0.77 and the other only 0.08. More samples can therefore help a lot, but early learning is unreliable. Three changes did not help, within seed noise: the relative DONE logit, a longer horizon (gamma 0.99, which clearly hurt) and the footprint-convolution head. Higher entropy (0.02) went with a full collapse to DONE in both round-1 trials that used it. The failures look like slow or unlucky discovery of the shift early in training. So this round tests a shared shift kernel that should make alignment faster and more reliable, plus a middle ground of 3 PPO epochs.
